entries.name: Khmer New Year (Choul Chnam Thmey)
entries.capsule: Three-day Cambodian New Year in mid-April marking the end of harvest; Minnesota temples celebrate on nearby weekends.
entries.dateRule: In Cambodia, usually April 13 or 14 to 16, set each year by the Cambodian government from the traditional astronomical calendar. Minnesota temples hold public celebrations on a weekend near or after these dates.
entries.whatItMarks: The traditional Khmer new year at the end of the dry-season harvest; families visit temples, make offerings to ancestors and monks, build sand hills and play traditional games.
entries.howCelebratedInMinnesota: At Watt Munisotaram (Empire Township, near Hampton) with processions and decorated halls; MNopedia shows a procession on April 16, 2016, and MPR reported the 40-acre site was bought to have room for big celebrations. In Rochester the Buddhist Support Society holds a separate weekend festival at Watt Dhamma Visudhikaram (see its own entry). University students have held their own New Year evening. No 2026 date for Watt Munisotaram was found.

entries.name: Cambodian New Year Celebration, Rochester (Buddhist Support Society)
entries.capsule: Rochester's public Khmer New Year weekend at Watt Dhamma Visudhikaram: monks' blessings, parade, dance, games, food vendors.
entries.dateRule: Announced each year by the Buddhist Support Society; recent years fell on the last full weekend of April, after Cambodia's April 14-16 holiday, because, organizers say, farmers finish the harvest first.

dates.source: KTTC, April 24, 2026 (Friday blessing; public Saturday-Sunday 9 a.m.-10 p.m.)

entries.whatItMarks: Khmer New Year, celebrated by Rochester's Cambodian Buddhist community.
entries.howCelebratedInMinnesota: Friday blessing by monks; public days open with a blessing and rice offering, then a parade with a Cambodian dance group, the passing of the New Year angel, live bands, games and more than 20 food and merchandise vendors (2026, KTTC). In 2025 (April 25-27) the program included food offerings to ancestors, sand hills, chanting, lunch for Buddhist followers, games, a blessing dance and the signing of a sister-city pact with Tboung Khmum Province (KIMT; KROC).

minnesotaEvents.place: Watt Dhamma Visudhikaram, 4462 29th St. SE, Rochester

entries.name: Visakha Bochea (Vesak)
entries.capsule: Theravada holy day for the Buddha's birth, enlightenment and death, marked with evening processions at Watt Munisotaram.
entries.dateRule: Full moon of the sixth lunar month (usually May); the Cambodian and Thai calendars can differ in years with an added lunar month, and temples may choose a nearby weekend. Seed dates follow the Thai calendar.
entries.whatItMarks: The birth, enlightenment and death of the Buddha in Theravada tradition.
entries.howCelebratedInMinnesota: MNopedia records Visakha Puja at Watt Munisotaram, with a procession and celebration photographed May 20, 2016. No 2026 date was announced on the temple's site.

minnesotaEvents.name: Visakha Puja at Watt Munisotaram
minnesotaEvents.organizerDates: May 20, 2016 (past example); no current date found

entries.name: Cambodian Genocide Remembrance Day
entries.capsule: April 17 recalls the Khmer Rouge seizure of Phnom Penh in 1975 and the nearly 2 million people killed by 1979.
entries.whatItMarks: The Khmer Rouge takeover of Phnom Penh on April 17, 1975, and the genocide that followed until January 1979.

sources.title: H.Res. 338, Cambodian Genocide Remembrance Day, U.S. House

entries.name: Pchum Ben
entries.capsule: Two weeks of offerings and prayers for ancestral spirits, ending in the main Pchum Ben day in September or October.
entries.dateRule: Last of fifteen days at the end of the Khmer lunar month Photrobot (Bhadrapada), usually September or October; the main day is the 15th day.
entries.whatItMarks: The end of a two-week period of offerings and prayers to ancestral spirits, following the lunar calendar.

sources.title: Pchum Ben Day, Tuol Sleng Genocide Museum

entries.name: Meak Bochea (Magha Puja)
entries.capsule: Theravada holy day recalling 1,250 disciples gathering before the Buddha; candlelit processions at Watt Munisotaram.
entries.dateRule: Full moon of the third lunar month, usually February or March; temples may hold it on the nearest weekend.
entries.whatItMarks: The gathering of 1,250 of the Buddha's first disciples and the setting of rules for the community, as the AP described it.
entries.howCelebratedInMinnesota: In early February 2023 (the weekend of Feb. 4), dozens in white joined a candlelit procession led by monks past the altar at Watt Munisotaram, with children carrying U.S., Cambodian and Buddhist flags, followed by two hours of chanting in Khmer (AP).

minnesotaEvents.name: Magha Puja at Watt Munisotaram
minnesotaEvents.organizerDates: Early February 2023 (past example); no current date found

entries.name: Asanha Bochea and start of Buddhist Lent (Chol Vassa)
entries.capsule: Full-moon holy day for the Buddha's first sermon; the next day begins monks' three-month rains retreat.
entries.dateRule: Full moon of the eighth lunar month, usually July; the rains retreat starts the next day. Seed dates follow the Thai calendar.
entries.whatItMarks: The Buddha's first sermon and the start of the three-month rains retreat.

entries.name: Cambodian Heritage Day (Minnesota)
entries.capsule: Cambodian American Partnership of Minnesota's day of classical dance, music, exhibits and Khmer food; held in 2023 and 2025.
entries.dateRule: Set by the Cambodian American Partnership of Minnesota; held Saturday, Sept. 23, 2023 and Saturday, Sept. 27, 2025. Not necessarily annual.
entries.whatItMarks: Cambodian heritage and, in 2025, 50 years of Cambodians in Minnesota.
entries.howCelebratedInMinnesota: 2023 at the Minnesota History Center, St. Paul, with dance, a fashion show, food and artifacts. 2025 at 1300 W. 106th St., Bloomington (Oak Grove Middle School): more than 900 guests, 41 vendors, 100 volunteers, blessings from Watt Munisotaram monks and a pastor, Wattanak and Romdoul dance troupes, and a proclamation from Gov. Tim Walz.
